items.title: Kevin Yu clubhouse leader in Austin as another round fails to finish
items.summary:
AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Kevin Yu at least managed to finish the second round Friday at the Austin Championship with another 6-under 66. Whether he keeps the lead is not nearly as important as how he finishes the PGA Tour's penultimate fall tournament.

Yu, who came into the week at No. 99 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, finished with two good par putts and was at 12-under 132.

Trace Crowe, the 18-hole leader who played in the afternoon, was at 13 under when play was suspended for the second straight day by darkness. Crowe faced a 55-foot birdie putt on the par-3 17th hole when play was to resume Saturday morning at Omni Barton Creek.

“If you think about it, it’s definitely a lot of pressure,” Yu said about the standings. "But on the golf course pressure’s not going to do anything good to you. I’m trying to just be myself on the course, try to hit good golf shots.

“If I just keep hitting good golf shots, the good golf is going to take care of itself.”

The PGA Tour season ends next week at Sea Island on the Georgia coast, and the top 100 are assured full status for 2027, a key year before the tour shifts its competitive model.

Brian Harman, whose 2023 British Open title came with a five-year exemption, had a 66 and was at 11-unde 133 along with Kristoffer Ventura (67), who also has status locked up for next year.

Crowe went 32 holes before finally making a bogey, going from the rough to well over the green on the 15th hole and missing a par putt from outside 20 feet. He finishes with a par 5 on Saturday, and the tour is hopeful Saturday will finish on time with a smaller…

The North Carolina State Board of Trustees has made it official, naming Philip Rivers to lead the Wolfpack football team in the coming years.

After weeks of speculation , the board officially announced that the former Wolfpack quarterback is the new head coach on Friday. Rivers signed a five-year deal.

"I gave it everything I had here as a player for 51 games, and I will give it everything I have as the coach," Rivers said Friday. "There's no denying that this is going to take hard work, but we're not scared of hard. I look forward to getting after it every single day with an unbelievable coaching staff and a group of players who are dedicated to relentlessly pursuing victory."

ABC11 first reported on Wednesday that the board would vote on the deal during Friday's meeting.

Rivers played quarterback at NC State from 2000 to 2003, and just wrapped up his sixth season as head coach of St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama. Rivers, who has never coached in college, led the Cardinals to the state playoff semifinals the previous two seasons.

"His love for this university is apparent (four) years ago when I met him. items.title: Lakers' Austin Reaves day-to-day with bruised heel, doesn't undergo imaging
items.summary:
Any Los Angeles Lakers game in which Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves both exit with injuries is going to be concerning, but it appears the team has dodged any serious fallout.

Two days after the Lakers’ two leading scorers left a win over the Milwaukee Bucks , head coach JJ Redick told reporters Friday that he expects Dončić to be available for Sunday’s game against the Phoenix Suns. Dončić had already told reporters he was “good” the night of the injury, which was a tweaked ankle.

As for Reaves, Redick said the guard was day-to-day with a bruise on his heel, but the matter is apparently minor enough the team didn’t even bother with imaging on the foot.

“AR, based on his physical evaluation and how he was feeling yesterday, we opted against imaging. He’ll be day-to-day. We’ll have him on the report tomorrow at 5 o’clock.“

Even with their early exits Friday, no pair of teammates is averaging more com,bined points per game than Dončić and Reaves. Dončić leads the league in scoring with 38.6 points per game, while Reaves if 15th with 24.7. Dončić is also ninth in the league in assists per game at 7.6.

Rotation guard Collin Sexton also exited Friday’s game a collision with Bucks guard Ryan Rollins. He needed stitches above his right eye, but Redick said a concussion was ruled out and he’s “probably in the same boat” as Reaves.

The Lakers-Suns game is scheduled for 1 p.m. PT on Sunday in Phoenix.

It is also the second straight year that a Greater Catholic League-Coed school has won both a boys and girls state championship. Perhaps the biggest surprise is that, while the men’s final in Brisbane is the one everyone expected, Australia and New Zealand are contesting it for the first time since 2013. items.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
items.summary:
Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival

It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player. You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball.

These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.
